chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Satan does not cease to be alarmed by the believer as long as he preserves upon the five prayers. But when he wastes them, he becomes audacious against him and leads him into grave sins.

key_terms.الصَّلَوَات الْخَمْس: The five obligatory daily prayers (salat) — Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha
key_terms.الْعَظَائِم: The major/grave sins — serious transgressions in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.ذَعِراً: Alarmed, frightened, in a state of panic — describes Satan's condition before a praying believer

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about protecting oneself from Satan through the five daily prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through al-Sakuni from Imam Sadiq (AS) who attributes it to the Prophet (SAWW), establishes a direct spiritual connection between maintaining the five daily prayers and protection from satanic influence. The Prophet uses the word 'ذَعِراً' (alarmed/frightened) to depict Satan as genuinely intimidated by a believer who regularly performs salat, suggesting that prayer creates an ongoing spiritual barrier. When the believer abandons this practice, Satan becomes emboldened and gains an entry point into the believer's heart, steering them toward major sins (al-'aza'im). The original audience — early Muslim communities in Kufa — would have understood this as both a spiritual warning and a practical reminder that prayer is the believer's first line of spiritual defense.
